Cycle Outcome questionnaire Use these exact section names as `section` values in `submit_cycle_outcome`. Allowed `status` values: `BLOCKED`, `FAILED`, `INCONCLUSIVE`, `NO_CHANGE_REQUIRED`, `PARTIALLY_REMEDIATED`, `READY_FOR_INDEPENDENT_VALIDATION`. Scope every self-validation claim to the properties its underlying check actually evaluated; a successful check does not establish a requirement, success criterion, constraint, or outcome that it did not evaluate, so keep that coverage unresolved or unverified. In Implementation Result, capture the actual final repository approach, requirement coverage, constraints, compatibility or regression implications, actual self-validation, unresolved or unverified coverage, and partial, blocked, failed, inconclusive, or no-change state when applicable. In Cycle Intent vs. Implementation, capture material deviations, causal evidence, materially attempted or reverted approaches, material assumption changes, the resulting strategy, and why it was selected when those events occurred. In Implementation Trail, chronologically capture material implementation and investigation actions, observed evidence, influential unsuccessful attempts, reassessment points, resulting changes, and self-validation. Self-validation is not authoritative deterministic validation. You may add clearly named, decision-relevant sections after all required sections. Required sections: - `Implementation Result`: What was actually implemented during this cycle, and what did your self-validation establish against the Task to Solve, including its success criteria and constraints? If no solution or only a partial solution was implemented, state that explicitly and identify what remains unresolved or unverified. - `Cycle Intent vs. Implementation`: Did the implemented solution materially differ from the selected strategy recorded in the Cycle Intent? If yes, what changed, what evidence or findings discovered during implementation led to the material reassessment, and why was the resulting strategy or solution selected? If there was no material change from the Cycle Intent, state that directly. - `Implementation Trail`: What was the actual sequence of material implementation and investigation actions from the Cycle Intent through self-validation? Execution response (compatibility evidence): The `mvn clean verify` command succeeded, confirming that the applied changes did not break the build (R3). The `scan_current_repository` results show that all vulnerabilities related to `org.apache.commons:commons-text`, `org.json:json`, `io.micrometer:micrometer-core`, `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core`, `tools.jackson.core:jackson-core`, and `tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind` (except one initially, which was subsequently fixed) have been resolved. Specifically: - `org.apache.commons:commons-text` was updated from `1.9` to `1.10.0`. - `org.json:json` was updated from `20230227` to `20231013`. - `io.micrometer:micrometer-core` was implicitly updated through `micrometer.version` to `1.16.6`. - `org.apache.tomcat.embed:tomcat-embed-core` was implicitly updated through `tomcat.version` to `11.0.25`. - `tools.jackson.core:jackson-core` was implicitly updated through `jackson.version` to `3.1.6`. - `tools.jackson.core:jackson-databind` was implicitly updated through `jackson.version` to `3.1.6`, resolving all related vulnerabilities. The remaining vulnerabilities are: - `org.springframework:spring-expression` (CVE-2026-41850) - `org.springframework:spring-webmvc` (CVE-2026-41845) - `org.springframework:spring-webmvc` (CVE-2026-41842) These Spring Framework vulnerabilities could not be addressed in this cycle because attempting to override the Spring Framework version (`spring-framework.version` property to `6.2.19`) with the non-standard `spring-boot-starter-parent:4.0.6` led to build failures (`NoClassDefFoundError`). Given the constraint of not allowing major version upgrades for Spring Boot and the inability to resolve `spring-boot-starter-parent:3.2.14` (which would be compatible with Spring Framework 6.x), a compatible fixed version for Spring Framework could not be safely introduced without further investigation into the custom `spring-boot-starter-parent:4.0.6` or external environmental issues regarding Maven artifact resolution. This means that while significant progress has been made, the solution is PARTIAL. Final Answer: The solution implemented addressed 17 out of 20 identified vulnerabilities. The remaining 3 vulnerabilities are related to Spring Framework and could not be resolved due to the use of a non-standard Spring Boot parent version (`4.0.6`) and the associated incompatibility when attempting to update Spring Framework dependencies.
